items.title: Section: Correct Practice Opens — Five Ways of Properly Dispelling the Object, and the Beginner's Method

items.zh: 云何名正加行？謂於所緣數起勝解，數正除遣，是名正加行。如有勤修不淨觀者，數正除遣於諸不淨作意思惟諸不淨相。由隨相行毘鉢舍那而起作意，於所緣境數數除遣，數數現前。其正除遣，復有五種。一、內攝其心故；二、不念作意故；三、於餘作意故；四、對治作意故；五、無相界作意故。
items.en: What is correct practice? That is, repeatedly generating vivid understanding with respect to the object, and repeatedly, correctly dispelling it — this is called correct practice. For instance, one who diligently cultivates contemplation of impurity repeatedly and correctly dispels, and directs attention to, various marks of impurity. This correct dispelling is, moreover, of five kinds: first, by gathering the mind inward; second, by non-attentive engagement; third, by engagement with a different object; fourth, by engagement as an antidote; fifth, by engagement with the markless realm.

items.zh: 當知此中，由九相心住、毘鉢舍那而為上首，故名內攝其心。由於最初背一切相，無亂安住，故名不念作意。由緣餘定地境，思惟餘定地，故名於餘作意。由思惟不淨對治於淨，乃至思惟阿那波那念對治尋思，思惟虛空界對治諸色，故名對治作意。由於一切相不作意思惟，於無相界作意思惟，故名無相界作意。
雖遍安立一切所緣正除遣相總有五種，然此義中，正意唯取內攝其心，不念作意。初修業者始修業時，最初全不於所緣境繫縛其心，或於不淨，或復餘處。唯作是念：我心云何得無散亂、無相、無分別、寂靜、極寂靜、無轉無動、無所希望、離諸作用、於內適悅？
items.en: Although the marks of correct dispelling, applied across every object, are five in total, the primary intent here takes up only the first two — gathering the mind inward and non-attentive engagement. When a beginner first takes up practice, at the very start he cannot bind the mind to the object at all … he can only reflect thus: "How may my mind become free of distraction, free of marks, free of discursive thought, tranquil, thoroughly tranquil, unmoving and unwavering, free of expectation, free of all effortful activity, and inwardly at ease?"

items.zh: 如是精勤，於所生起一切外相無所思惟，不念作意；即由如是不念作意，除遣所緣。彼於其中修習瑜伽，攝受適悅。復行有相、有分別不淨等境。云何而行？謂由隨相行、隨尋思行、隨伺察行毘鉢舍那，行彼境界，而非一向精勤修習毘鉢舍那。還捨觀相，復於所緣思惟止行。由是因緣，彼於爾時，於所緣境不捨、不取。由於所緣止行轉故，不名為捨；即於所緣不作相故，無分別故，不名為取。即由如是內攝其心，除遣所緣。又於其中不取觀相故，於緣無亂；取止行故，而復緣於所知事相。

items.title: Section: Gathering the Mind Inward, and the Painter's Apprentice

items.zh: 若於所緣唯數勝解，不數除遣；即不令彼所有勝解後後明淨究竟而轉，不能往趣乃至現觀所知境事。由數勝解、數除遣故，後後勝解展轉明淨究竟而轉，亦能往趣乃至現觀所知境事。
items.en: If, with respect to the object, one only repeatedly generates vivid understanding without repeatedly dispelling it, then one's successive understandings never become progressively clearer and more refined, and one is unable to proceed all the way to directly witnessing the object of knowledge. But through repeatedly generating vivid understanding and repeatedly dispelling it, each successive understanding becomes progressively clearer and more refined, and one is thereby able to proceed all the way to directly witnessing the object of knowledge.

items.zh: 譬如世間畫師弟子，初習畫業，先從師所受所學樣。諦觀諦觀，作彼形相；作已作已，尋即除毀；既除毀已，尋復更作。如如除毀，數數更作，如是如是後後形相轉明、轉淨究竟顯現。如是正學，經歷多時，世共推許為大畫師，或墮師數。若不數除所作形相，即於其上數數重畫，便於形相永無明淨究竟顯期。
items.en: It is like a painter's apprentice in the world: newly taking up the craft of painting, he first receives from his teacher a model to study. Gazing at it carefully, again and again, he renders its form; having rendered it, he then promptly destroys it; having destroyed it, he promptly renders it once more. As he destroys it again and again, and renders it again and again, each successive form becomes ever clearer, ever more refined, until it is perfectly displayed … But if he does not repeatedly destroy what he has rendered, and instead simply paints over it again and again on the same surface, the form will never have any hope of becoming clear and refined to completion.

items.title: Section: Correct Practice Closes — Fixed and Flexible Objects, Coarse and Subtle Images, and All Nine Practices Complete

items.zh: 若於此境起勝解已，定於此境復正除遣；非於此境正除遣已，定於此境復起勝解。於狹小境起勝解已，即於狹小而正除遣。廣大、無量、當知亦爾。於狹小境正除遣已，或於狹小復起勝解，或於廣大復起勝解，或於無量復起勝解。
items.en: If one has generated vivid understanding with respect to a given object, one must then correctly dispel that same object — but having correctly dispelled a given object, one is not thereby bound to generate vivid understanding of that same object again. Having generated vivid understanding of a small object, one correctly dispels that same small object — and the same holds for a vast or a boundless object. Having correctly dispelled a small object, one may generate vivid understanding again of a small object, or of a vast object, or of a boundless object.

items.zh: 於其廣大及於無量，當知亦爾。
若諸色法所有相貌影像顯現，當知是麁，變化相似。諸無色法假名為先，如所領受增上力故，影像顯現。如是一切名正加行。如是九種白品加行，於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，當知隨順。
items.en: Whatever image appears bearing the marks of a form-possessing phenomenon should be known as coarse, its transformations closely resembling their original. Formless phenomena, preceded by provisional naming, appear as images through the empowering force of what has been apprehended of them. All of this is called correct practice. These nine kinds of bright-category preparatory practice should be known as conducive to both calm-abiding and insight.

items.title: Section: Locus Three, One-Pointedness of Mind, Closes — Eighteen Practices in Total

items.zh: 與是相違九種加行，於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，當知違逆。如是黑品、白品差別建立加行，有十八種。如是名為心一境性。
items.en: The nine kinds of preparatory practice that are the reverse of these should be known as obstructing both calm-abiding and insight. Thus, the preparatory practices established as differentiated into the dark and bright categories number eighteen in total. This is called one-pointedness of mind.

blocks.text: The last and subtlest of the nine good practices: how to form a meditative image and then let it go. A passage (0456c23) is untranslated.

"Repeatedly generating vivid understanding of the object, and repeatedly, correctly dispelling it." Five ways to dispel: gathering the mind inward; non-attention; attending to another object; attending to an antidote; attending to the markless realm. Here the first two are meant.
A beginner "cannot bind the mind to the object at once". So he takes up the image, then lets it go.

With diligence, one stops attending to outer signs and so dispels the object; one then alternates: practising insight on the image with its features (following the mark, investigation, examination), then setting the image aside and returning to calm. Thus "one neither abandons nor grasps the object": not abandoning, since calm continues on it; not grasping, since one forms no sign or discrimination of it.

If one only forms the image without dispelling it, the understanding never becomes clearer. "It is like a painter's apprentice: he copies the teacher's model, then rubs it out; copies it again, and rubs it out again. If he simply painted over it, it would never become clear." Each new image becomes clearer than the last.
After a small object, a middling one; after middling, a large one. Images of form are "coarse"; images of formless phenomena, built on names, are subtle.
Nine bright and nine dark: "this is called one-pointedness of mind", the third locus.

quiz.q: Of the five ways of dispelling, only the first two are meant here. Why, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: beginners have strong torpor and distraction — these two counter them
quiz.why: "The primary intent here takes up only the first two — gathering the mind inward and non-attentive engagement." Venerable Miào Jìng: beginners have strong torpor and strong distraction, so these are meant to counter that.

quiz.q: The fifth way of dispelling is "engagement with the markless realm." What is the markless realm?
options: the state beyond all marks — suchness; contemplating suchness
quiz.why: "Fourth, by engagement as an antidote; fifth, by engagement with the markless realm." Venerable Miào Jìng: the markless realm, beyond all marks, is suchness. Master Cháng Bǎi likewise calls it engagement with suchness.

quiz.q: Through repeated generating and dispelling, "one proceeds all the way to directly witnessing the object." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say direct witnessing is?
options: non-discursive wisdom appears — entering the noble path
quiz.why: "Through repeatedly generating vivid understanding and repeatedly dispelling it, each successive understanding becomes progressively clearer and more refined, and one is thereby able to proceed all the way to directly witnessing the object of knowledge." Venerable Miào Jìng: "directly witnessing the object" means non-discursive wisdom has appeared — one has entered the noble path.

quiz.q: If the painter's apprentice doesn't keep erasing, what happens, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: painting over the same sheet without starting fresh, it just gets dirtier
quiz.why: "If he does not repeatedly destroy what he has rendered, and instead simply paints over it again and again on the same surface, the form will never become clear and refined." Master Cháng Bǎi: not tearing it up to start over, painting again and again on the same sheet — it just gets dirtier.

quiz.q: "Having generated understanding of a small object, one dispels it." Why does Venerable Miào Jìng say beginners start small?
options: at first the mind lacks strength — keep the object small, e.g., one skeleton
quiz.why: "Having generated vivid understanding of a small object, one correctly dispels that same small object." Venerable Miào Jìng: at first your mental strength is insufficient, so don't make the object too vast — keep it small; contemplating bones, contemplate just one skeleton.

quiz.q: Images of form "should be known as coarse." How does Master Cháng Bǎi compare form and formless images?
options: form images are coarser, formless images subtler
quiz.why: "Whatever image appears bearing the marks of a form-possessing phenomenon should be known as coarse." Master Cháng Bǎi: images of form are coarser; images of formless phenomena are subtler.

quiz.q: How many preparatory practices are there in all, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng sum up?
options: nine dark and nine bright — eighteen — called one-pointedness
quiz.why: "Thus, the preparatory practices established as differentiated into the dark and bright categories number eighteen in total. This is called one-pointedness of mind." Venerable Miào Jìng: nine dark and nine bright — eighteen — called one-pointedness of mind.
